text:
The Kraken made their big decision of the season before they left for Finland: Shane Wright, the fourth overall pick in 2022, went to Nashville for Matthew Wood. Moves like that say who a team believes in, and in Seattle that looks like Berkly Catton, who has 10 points in his last 10 games and an eight-game point streak that drew a headline asking whether he's the star the Kraken have been waiting for. Catton played on Wright's line before the trade; how Lane Lambert rebuilds that line is the thing to watch.

The uncomfortable part is the gap between the standings and the play. Seattle is 9-7-1 with 19 points, but it has had only 45% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances) and has scored about nine more goals than its chances deserved. Our numbers say the Kraken have earned about 15 points, not 19, and give them a 28% shot at the playoffs. Thursday's 4-1 loss to Carolina in Helsinki, outshot 30-13, looked like the underlying numbers catching up in a single afternoon.

The goaltending isn't covering it either. Philipp Grubauer is at .863 over his last five starts and Joey Daccord at .865 over his, and Daccord was pulled against the Rangers last week. Bobby McMann has one point in 10 games on 5.1 expected goals, which at least is a slump the chances say should turn.
